NDT training near Fort Worth: Tarrant County College, employer training and online study with a hands-on practical compared

Fort Worth is one of the Texas cities where a near-me search for NDT training has a genuine local college answer: Tarrant County College teaches nondestructive inspection at its Northwest Campus, with a programme contact at its aviation centre by Alliance Airport. Beyond the college, Fort Worth candidates choose between learning on the job with an inspection company or manufacturer, a welding-inspection degree across the Metroplex in Irving, and online theory paired with a practical at their employer. Here is how those routes compare.

Who offers NDT training around Fort Worth?

  • Tarrant County College, Northwest Campus. The Nondestructive Inspection, Testing and Evaluation programme offers a 60-credit-hour AAS, a 26-credit NDT Technician certificate and a 19-credit Radiography Technician certificate, covering ultrasonic, eddy current, radiographic, magnetic particle and penetrant inspection for aerospace, aviation, oil and gas, defence, power and transport employers. There are no prerequisites and you can start in fall, spring or summer, but classes run in person on Monday-to-Thursday mornings and each course is offered once every two years. The contact point is TCC's Center of Excellence in Aviation, Transportation & Logistics at Alliance Airport.
  • TCC continuing education. A working Fort Worth technician who needs one method rather than a degree can look at the non-credit courses: Eddy Current Technician, Liquid Penetrant/Magnetic Particle Technician, Radiographic Inspector and Ultrasound Technician. Their length varies by course.
  • Employers that hire against documented hours. A Sabre Industries posting for an NDT technician in Fort Worth, revised in 2024, asked for a visual weld inspector meeting AWS D1.1, MT with 20 classroom hours and 280 verifiable on-the-job hours, UT with 80 classroom hours and 840 on-the-job hours, all referenced to SNT-TC-1A, plus a Jaeger J-2 near-vision test with red/yellow colour distinction. Those are the Level I plus Level II totals in SNT-TC-1A's recommended tables, and the posting expected them on paper before the interview.
  • Tulsa Welding School, Irving. The Dallas Metro campus teaches an AAS in Welding Inspection and Quality Management on top of its welder programme. It covers codes, inspection procedures and metallurgy; the description names no individual NDT methods.
  • ASNT North Texas Section. The local ASNT section for the Metroplex, and a practical way to meet Fort Worth Level IIIs, aerospace quality staff and inspection-company managers.

Which Fort Worth route fits you?

Your situationRoute that usually fitsWhat to watch
No NDT job yet, mornings freeTCC's NDT Technician certificate or AASThe two-year course rotation decides how fast you finish
Already on a shop floor or flight lineA TCC continuing-education method course, or online theory with an employer practicalWhether your employer's written practice accepts the record
Applying to a posting like Sabre'sClassroom hours for MT and UT, documented, plus logged experienceHours must be verifiable, not just claimed
Fort Worth employer certifying a crewOn-site training with Level III-run exams under a written practiceVision exams, exam grading and record keeping

Questions to ask any NDT training provider near Fort Worth

  • Do the hours add up? Ask for classroom hours by method and level and compare them with the SNT-TC-1A totals using the SNT-TC-1A hours planner.
  • What do you practise on? Welds, castings and machined parts with real flaws teach far more than reference blocks alone.
  • Who certifies? A course record certifies nobody. Your Fort Worth employer certifies you under its written practice; ASNT certifies only through its own exams.
  • Does it fit your shift? Weekday-morning attendance works for some manufacturing schedules and rules out others.
  • Who checks vision? Near-vision and colour-contrast exams sit inside your employer's written practice; the SNT-TC-1A eligibility checker explains what is needed.
  • Who answers questions? Is an ASNT NDT Level III reachable while you train, and who writes the exams you will sit?

Where Atlantis fits for Fort Worth candidates and employers

Nothing in the Atlantis route needs a trip across town. Atlantis NDT has no classroom in Fort Worth; method theory is read online on the Atlantis portal, an ASNT NDT Level III answers course questions, and you can enrol on any day of the year. Set-up and scanning are practised in the Practical NDT simulator, and the hands-on practical and practical exam run at your employer's own shop, hangar or yard on its equipment, under a written practice built on SNT-TC-1A, with certification issued by your employer. Useful starting points: NDT Level 1, NDT Level 2, UT, MT and eddy current training.

Fort Worth manufacturers and inspection companies that want training delivered on-site, plus a written practice and Level III-administered exams, can start with SNT-TC-1A training programme set-up. Weld inspectors can add the six-day AWS CWI exam prep for Fort Worth. Nearby pages: Dallas, Oklahoma City and NDT training in Texas.
